findings.title: getTintSources reports a tint source for every LiquidBlock, including untinted fluids (lava, most modded fluids)
findings.detail: Upstream dev returns null when the fluid state model has no tint source (git show dev: ModelFactory.getTintSources -> 'if (tintSource == null) return null'). The port unconditionally returns List.of(IClientFluidTypeExtensions.of(fluidState).getTintColor(...)), and IClientFluidTypeExtensions.DEFAULT.getTintColor() returns 0xFFFFFFFF (-1) for fluids without a client extension override (ref IClientFluidTypeExtensions.java:60,262; the lava extension in ClientNeoForgeMod.java:135+ does not override the 3-arg getTintColor). Consequences for lava-like fluids: tintSources != null, so processTextureBakeResult sets modelFlags bit 0 ('has tint', ModelFactory.java:648) and runs TextureUtils.computeFaceTint per face (line 622-629) where dev skipped both; the uploaded colour is entry.tintingColour = captureColourConstant(..) -> -1 | 0xFF000000 = -1. No visible effect today: no shader reads flagsA bit 0 (grep of assets/voxy/shaders: only bits 2/4/8 are read in block_model.glsl:34-44; quad_util.glsl:93 treats colourTint == uint(-1) as 'no tint'), and the per-face tint bits stay 0 because the fluid getter's getBlockTint (which sets vertex meta bit 4) is never called for untinted fluids. It is a latent divergence from dev's model-buffer contents rather than a runtime bug.
findings.evidence: ModelFactory.java:806-812 (port), dev ModelFactory.getTintSources ('if (tintSource == null) return null'), ref/mc/net/neoforged/neoforge/client/extensions/common/IClientFluidTypeExtensions.java:60 and :262 (default 0xFFFFFFFF), ref/mc/net/neoforged/neoforge/client/ClientNeoForgeMod.java:130-136 (only water overrides the 3-arg getTintColor), src/main/resources/assets/voxy/shaders/lod/block_model.glsl:34-44 (flagsA bits 2,4,8 only), quad_util.glsl:93
findings.proposedFix: Mirror dev's null contract: in the LiquidBlock branch, probe the extension once with the non-biome getter (captureColourConstant-style) and return null when the extension is IClientFluidTypeExtensions.DEFAULT or when getTintColor returns -1 without calling getBlockTint; e.g. `var ext = IClientFluidTypeExtensions.of(fs); if (ext == IClientFluidTypeExtensions.DEFAULT) return null;` before building the list.

findings.title: PREPARED ThreadLocal is never cleared when VoxyInstance() throws DontCreateInstance
findings.detail: The Java 21 rewrite hands the pre-super() state to shouldCreateInstance() through the static ThreadLocal PREPARED: prepare() calls PREPARED.set(state) (line 57), the private constructor calls super() (line 40) and only then PREPARED.remove() (line 41). VoxyInstance's constructor evaluates shouldCreateInstance() first and throws DontCreateInstance when the storage config has disabled=true (VoxyInstance.java:35-37); VoxyCommon.createInstance() catches that exception (VoxyCommon.java:82-84). On that path line 41 is never reached, so the PreparedState record (Config + resolved Path) stays attached to the render thread for the rest of the session. There is no functional error today because every construction goes through prepare() first, which overwrites the slot, but the invariant 'ThreadLocal is only populated during construction' silently breaks on the very configuration (disabled storage) the mechanism exists to honour.
findings.evidence: VoxyClientInstance.java:35-46 (this(prepare()) -> super() -> PREPARED.remove()), :48-59 (prepare() sets PREPARED before returning), :62-67 (shouldCreateInstance reads PREPARED.get()); VoxyInstance.java:34-37 (throws DontCreateInstance from the super constructor before any other statement); VoxyCommon.java:80-84 (createInstance catches DontCreateInstance, so the stale value survives). Upstream dev (git diff dev) had no ThreadLocal: the prologue ran before super() and shouldCreateInstance read this.config directly.
findings.proposedFix: Make shouldCreateInstance() the single point that consumes and clears the slot: `var state = PREPARED.get(); PREPARED.remove(); var config = state != null ? state.config : this.config; return config == null || !config.disabled;` and drop the PREPARED.remove() at line 41 (or keep it as a harmless no-op). Every path through VoxyInstance() calls shouldCreateInstance() exactly once, so this clears the ThreadLocal whether or not the super constructor throws.

findings.title: Every production dedicated-server start logs an ERROR with a NoClassDefFoundError stack trace from CpuLayout.<clinit>
findings.detail: On the user's Linux dedicated server LWJGL core is absent (brief C11), so Platform.get() at line 140 throws NoClassDefFoundError. The catch(Throwable) at line 146 is correct for safety, but it reports the expected condition through Logger.error("Failed to generate cpu core layout, falling back to null: ", t), which prints an ERROR line plus the full NoClassDefFoundError stack trace (Logger.java:53-54 passes the throwable to slf4j). This clinit is reached on every server start because Voxy World Gen V2 does Class.forName("me.cortex.voxy.client.config.VoxyConfig") (initialising) whose field initialiser calls CpuLayout.getCoreCount() (VoxyConfig.java:43). The dev-run log does not show it because the userdev classpath ships LWJGL (the file's own comment at line 137 acknowledges this). Behaviour is otherwise correct (CORES==null -> availableProcessors()), but an ERROR-level stack trace at boot is misleading for server operators and will be mistaken for a real failure. ThreadUtils.java:31-33 already handles the identical situation at INFO level without a stack trace.
findings.evidence: CpuLayout.java:138-149 (catch Throwable -> Logger.error(..., t)); Logger.java:42-58 (error() logs the throwable and, on the server, skips the HUD); VoxyConfig.java:43 (`serviceThreads = (int) Math.max(CpuLayout.getCoreCount()/1.5, 1)` runs in the instance initialiser executed by loadOrCreate() in <clinit>, line 37/124); scratchpad/ref/vwg2/out/VoxyIntegration.java:80-84 (Class.forName + getMethod("isEnabled") on the server); ThreadUtils.java:27-33 (INFO-level handling of the same NoClassDefFoundError).
findings.proposedFix: Distinguish the expected case from real failures: `catch (NoClassDefFoundError | UnsatisfiedLinkError e) { Logger.info("LWJGL not present (" + e.getClass().getSimpleName() + "), cpu core layout unavailable; using availableProcessors()"); } catch (Throwable t) { Logger.error("Failed to generate cpu core layout, falling back to null: ", t); }` (keeps the Throwable-safe contract from C11 and the prior port).

findings.title: Default `jar` artifact is not bootable on the production dedicated server (nested lwjgl-lmdb/zstd keep `requires transitive org.lwjgl`)
findings.detail: The plain `jar` task (build.gradle:258-270) bundles `META-INF/jarjar/lwjgl-lmdb-3.3.3.jar` and `lwjgl-zstd-3.3.3.jar` unmodified. Both are Multi-Release jars carrying `META-INF/versions/9/module-info.class` = `module org.lwjgl.lmdb { requires transitive org.lwjgl; ... }`. FML resolves the GAME module layer eagerly, so on a server that has no LWJGL core the layer fails to resolve at boot with `java.lang.module.FindException: Module org.lwjgl not found, required by org.lwjgl.lmdb` (the exact crash the prior port's build.gradle documents). The user's dedicated server has no LWJGL: `E:/RMN/Server/libraries/org` contains only antlr, apache, checkerframework, codehaus, jline, joml, lz4, openjdk, ow2, slf4j. Only the separate `slimJar` task (build.gradle:286-372, default `slimStripModuleInfo=lwjgl-lmdb,lwjgl-zstd`) strips the descriptors; the obvious artifact `build/libs/voxy-0.2.19-beta-02dfb1b.jar` (89 MB) does not. The orchestrator's dedicated-server smoke test (`runServer`, scratchpad/runserver_r3.log) cannot catch this because ModDevGradle puts LWJGL core on the userdev classpath and never goes through jar-in-jar. Everything else server-side was verified clean (see coverage), so this is the one thing that would still take the real server down.
findings.evidence: `unzip -l build/libs/voxy-0.2.19-beta-02dfb1b.jar` -> META-INF/jarjar/lwjgl-lmdb-3.3.3.jar (35187 B), lwjgl-zstd-3.3.3.jar; extracted nested lwjgl-lmdb-3.3.3.jar contains `META-INF/versions/9/module-info.class` (215 B, 2023-09-16); slim jar's nested copies are 37352/89855 B (rewritten, descriptor removed). build.gradle:273-280 comment: 'a dedicated server (which ships no LWJGL core) would otherwise die at boot with "Module org.lwjgl not found, required by org.lwjgl.lmdb"'. Prior port build.gradle:463-464 records the same JPMS conflict. Server libraries listing: `ls E:/RMN/Server/libraries/org` has no lwjgl directory. G7 impl report unresolved item #1 asked G0 to strip these descriptors; only slimJar does.
findings.proposedFix: Make the server-deployable artifact the default: either apply the module-info stripping (and the platform-native trimming) inside the `jar` task itself for the two LWJGL binding jars (automatic module `lwjgl.lmdb` reads every module, so the client keeps working exactly as the slim jar does), or wire `build`/`assemble` to depend on `slimJar` and name the plain jar with a `-dev`/`-fat` classifier so it cannot be mistaken for the deployable one. At minimum add an explicit deployment note: ONLY `voxy-0.2.19-beta-neoforge-1.21.1-slim.jar` goes into E:/RMN/Server/mods (and the client).

findings.title: Client mods folder still ships rmn-lodresync-1.0.0.jar (+ Roxy + voxy-0.2.16 Fabric jar): duplicate `voxy:lod_resync_*` payload registration aborts client mod loading once the native port is installed
findings.detail: The native port's `VoxyNetworkRegistration` registers `voxy:lod_resync_ready` / `voxy:lod_resync_request` under channel version "1" on the MOD bus. The user's client (E:/RMN/Client/mods) currently contains `rmn-lodresync-1.0.0.jar`, whose `io.rmn.lodresync.net.ResyncNetwork` registers the SAME two payload ids with `PROTOCOL_VERSION = "1"` (it exists only to provide the client half against the Roxy-bridged upstream 0.2.16 jar). With both mods present NeoForge's `NetworkRegistry.register` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Cannot register payload voxy:lod_resync_ready as it is already registered.")` (ref/mc NetworkRegistry.java:177) inside `RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent`, which is a mod-loading error screen. rmn-lodresync's `lodresync.mixins.json` also carries its own `MixinWorldgenClientQueue` (double redirect of the same `ArrayDeque.pollFirst` call sites) and a `MixinVoxyShutdown` written against the 0.2.16 class layout. Likewise `roxy-1.21.1-NeoForge-0.2.0.jar` and `voxy-0.2.16-beta+1.21.11.jar` (modId `voxy`) cannot coexist with the port (duplicate mod id / Roxy bytecode remapping of the wrong jar). None of this is caught by the orchestrator's dev-run smoke tests, which do not load the user's mods folder.
findings.evidence: `ls E:/RMN/Client/mods` -> rmn-lodresync-1.0.0.jar, roxy-1.21.1-NeoForge-0.2.0.jar, voxy-0.2.16-beta+1.21.11.jar; E:/RMN/Client/logs/latest.log:272,791 ('RMN LOD Resync 1.0.0 (lodresync)'); javap scratchpad/lodresync/io/rmn/lodresync/net/ResyncNetwork: `public static final String PROTOCOL_VERSION = "1"; onRegisterPayloads(RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent)`; ResyncPayloads$ResyncReady(int radiusChunks,int serveRatePerSecond)/ResyncRequest(long[]) with TYPE fields; scratchpad/lodresync/lodresync.mixins.json client:[MixinWorldgenClientQueue, MixinVoxyShutdown]; its neoforge.mods.toml depends optionally on voxy/roxy/voxyworldgenv2. Port side: VoxyNetworkRegistration.java:24 PROTOCOL_VERSION="1", :36-40 registrar("1").optional().playToClient/playToServer with LodResyncPayloads TYPEs (ids voxy:lod_resync_ready / voxy:lod_resync_request, LodResyncPayloads.java:41,51). NetworkRegistry.java:177 throws on duplicate registration.
findings.proposedFix: Add to the deployment procedure (README/PORTING-NOTES and the release notes): when installing the native jar on the client, delete `rmn-lodresync-1.0.0.jar`, `roxy-1.21.1-NeoForge-0.2.0.jar` and `voxy-0.2.16-beta+1.21.11.jar`. findings.title: Chunky config plugin lives inside the common mixin package prefix; gating survives only because Mixin selects all Voxy configs in one pass
findings.detail: ChunkyMixinPlugin is in package me.cortex.voxy.commonImpl.mixin.chunky, which starts with the mixin package of common.voxy.mixins.json (me.cortex.voxy.commonImpl.mixin). In the shipped sponge-mixin 0.15.2+mixin.0.8.7 (used by NeoForge 21.1.248, see runserver_r3.log:17) MixinProcessor.applyMixins throws NoClassDefFoundError('%s is in a defined mixin package %s* owned by %s and cannot be referenced directly') for any class loaded through the transformer whose name package-matches a config already in `configs`. The plugin class is loaded by MixinConfig.onSelect (new PluginHandle -> IClassProvider.findClass) during MixinProcessor.selectConfigs, which calls onSelect() BEFORE the config is appended and before `configs` is repopulated, so in the current setup (all five Voxy configs registered from neoforge.mods.toml and selected in the same DEFAULT-phase pass) no Voxy config is in `configs` while the plugin loads, and the Chunky-equipped dev server run shows no error. If the selection were ever split across passes (a config registered later, e.g. by another mod's plugin adding configs, or a phase change), PluginHandle catches the error, logs 'Error loading companion plugin class ... The plugin may be out of date', sets plugin=null and the @Pseudo mixin is then applied UNGATED (Chunky present: fine; absent: silently skipped). This is fragility, not a current failure. The Iris and worldgen plugins avoid it by living in client/compat.

findings.title: Sections added through Sodium's immediate-presentation path miss the visible-section bound store for one frame
findings.detail: The port resets VoxyRenderSystem.visbleSectionStream only at the HEAD of RenderSectionManager.createTerrainRenderList (MixinRenderSectionManager.java:53-59) and repopulates it from SectionCollector.visit(RenderSection,int) (MixinSectionCollector.java:20-27). In Sodium 0.8.13 createTerrainRenderList runs only when needsUpdate() is true (SodiumWorldRenderer.setupTerrain, src/sodium/.../SodiumWorldRenderer.java:226-229), but RenderSectionManager.processChunkBuildResults (RenderSectionManager.java:436-449) also calls sectionCollector.visitWithFlags(...) for blocking / immediate-presentation build results AFTER update(), in frames where no graph rebuild happened. Those calls reach the hook and StreamedBoundStore.put(), but put() never sets didChange (StreamedBoundStore.java:40-47) and preRender() uploads only when didChange is true (StreamedBoundStore.java:23-33), so the section is rendered by Sodium this frame while Voxy's bound store (used to cull LOD geometry inside vanilla-loaded volumes) still lacks it; the next frame's graph rebuild (needsGraphUpdate |= touchedSectionInfo, RenderSectionManager.java:380/434) resets and re-uploads it. Dev on Sodium 0.9 reset the stream every time a VisibleChunkCollector was created (renderOutOfGraph HEAD / readRenderListFromTree), so a put always followed a reset and the lag did not exist there. Net effect: a one-frame LOD/vanilla overlap flash at a section that was just built near the camera (piston pushes, nearby rebuilds, initial loads within 64 blocks).

findings.title: getBoundFramebufferTextures() silently degrades when the bound FBO has non-texture attachments (LODs vanish or land in the wrong target)
findings.detail: The C3 helper only validates the depth attachment. Two silent failure paths exist: (a) depth is a texture but GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 is a renderbuffer/absent -> getBoundAttachmentTexture returns 0, the value is returned as colourTexture and AbstractRenderPipeline.runPipeline (lines 141-143) binds scratchFramebuffer(GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 = 0); the final NormalRenderPipeline.finish blit then targets an incomplete FBO (draw buffer COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 with no image) and is dropped with GL_INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION - no log, LODs simply do not appear; (b) depth is not a texture (or fb 0 is bound) -> the code composites into Minecraft.getMainRenderTarget() while the pass actually draws into a different FBO, so Voxy's opaque output goes to the wrong target and its depth/stencil setup reads the wrong depth. Upstream 12111 (VoxyRenderSystem.java:239-241 in the scratchpad copy) threw IllegalStateException("Cannot use the default framebuffer as cannot source from it") instead of guessing. Vanilla RenderTarget (ref RenderTarget.java:119-127) and Iris GlFramebuffer always attach textures, so the user's setup is unaffected; the risk is third-party FBOs (camera/portal/mirror mods) that render the terrain layers with renderbuffer attachments.
findings.evidence: VoxyRenderSystem.java:454-488 (only depth==0 triggers the fallback; colour 0 passes through), AbstractRenderPipeline.java:140-143 (scratchFramebuffer.bind(GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, sourceColourTexture) with no completeness check), NormalRenderPipeline.java:135-139 (blit into outputFramebuffer), upstream_12111 VoxyRenderSystem.java lines ~236-241 (throws on fb 0), ref/mc/com/mojang/blaze3d/pipeline/RenderTarget.java:119-127 (main target attaches GL_TEXTURE_2D).
findings.proposedFix: Treat a non-texture GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 the same way as a non-texture depth (fall back to the main target only when BOTH attachments come from it, otherwise throw/skip the frame with a one-time Logger.error), and/or call scratchFramebuffer.verify() once after (re)binding in runPipeline so the failure is loud instead of an invisible LOD layer.

findings.title: Wall-fog classification uses the event's vanilla FogData values, so a NeoForge modded-fluid fog (camera inside a fluid with FogType.NONE) is overridden and removed
findings.detail: NeoForge's ClientHooks.onFogRender first lets IClientFluidTypeExtensions.of(state).modifyFogRender(...) adjust RenderSystem fog directly when the camera is inside ANY fluid block (modded fluids report FogType.NONE from Camera.getFluidInCamera(), which only knows WATER/LAVA/POWDER_SNOW), and only then posts ViewportEvent.RenderFog with the ORIGINAL vanilla FogData near/far. VoxyFogEvents gates on event.getType() != FogType.NONE (misses modded fluids) and computes isRenderDistanceFog from event.getFarPlaneDistance() (the untouched wall value), so it cancels the event with 1e9/1e9 and ClientHooks re-applies those to RenderSystem, discarding the fluid's custom fog. Result on 1.21.1 in the default FOG_AND_FADE mode: submerged in a modded fluid with its own fog (e.g. Mekanism/Create/IE fluids), the fog is removed for vanilla terrain, entities and Voxy LODs. On 26.2 (dev MixinFogRenderer) such a fluid fog is an environmental fog and is kept in FOG_AND_FADE/FOG.
findings.evidence: ref/mc/net/neoforged/neoforge/client/ClientHooks.java:447-458 (modifyFogRender before the event; event constructed with the vanilla nearDistance/farDistance; values re-applied only from the event when cancelled), ref/mc/net/minecraft/client/renderer/FogRenderer.java:220-283 (FogType branches only for LAVA/POWDER_SNOW/WATER, else wall branch), VoxyFogEvents.java:75-101 (uses event near/far + getType()), git show dev:...MixinFogRenderer.java:24-32 (dev keeps environmental fog unless removesVanillaEnvFog).
findings.proposedFix: Before classifying, also read the post-fluid-extension values from RenderSystem.getShaderFogStart()/getShaderFogEnd() (or replicate ClientHooks' fluid check: camera.getEntity().level().getFluidState(camera.getBlockPosition()) non-empty and camera y below the fluid height) and return early when they differ from the event's vanilla values or a fluid is present, so a fluid-provided fog is treated like the FogType != NONE case.

findings.title: C2 fog push is applied inside NeoForge's RenderFog event and can be overwritten by sodium-extra's setupFog TAIL injection, fogging out all LODs
findings.detail: VoxyFogEvents pushes the vanilla fog wall to 1e9 through ViewportEvent.RenderFog, which ClientHooks.onFogRender applies via RenderSystem.setShaderFogStart/End (ref ClientHooks.java:454-458) from the LAST statement of FogRenderer.setupFog (ref FogRenderer.java:282). sodium-extra 0.9.3 (installed on the user's client: E:/RMN/Client/mods/sodium-extra-neoforge-0.9.3+mc1.21.1.jar) injects at @At("TAIL") of the same method (javap -v me.flashyreese.mods.sodiumextra.mixin.fog.MixinFogRenderer: @Inject(method="setupFog", at=@At(value="TAIL"))) and, for FOG_TERRAIN with no fluid/effect/boss fog, calls sodiumExtra$applyTerrainFog: when distanceChunks != 0 it unconditionally does setShaderFogStart(getStart(..)); setShaderFogEnd(getEnd(distanceChunks)) (bytecode offsets 54-69), replacing Voxy's 1e9 values AFTER the event ran. MixinDefaultChunkRenderer then feeds VoxyFogParameters.current() (post-TAIL values) to setupViewport, so NormalRenderPipeline.finish (NormalRenderPipeline.java:102-117) fogs the LOD blit from that start to end and blit_texture_depth_cutout.frag:54-58 clamps everything beyond `end` to solid fog colour - i.e. every LOD beyond the sodium-extra fog distance disappears, exactly the failure C2/Roxy were designed to avoid. With the user's CURRENT sodium-extra config (distance_chunks: 0, start_percent: 100) the multiplier path re-writes the same 1e9 values (offsets 9-26), so it happens to work today, but any change of the 'Fog distance' slider (or the same hook being used for sodium-extra's cloud fog lambda, which calls setupFog(FOG_TERRAIN) and also re-fires the Voxy event) silently breaks LOD rendering. Roxy's RoxyFogRendererMixin hooked the same TAIL, so this is inherited fragility, but the native port has a better place to make it robust.
findings.evidence: VoxyFogEvents.java:70-102 (event handler, LOWEST priority, receiveCanceled); ref/mc/net/minecraft/client/renderer/FogRenderer.java:279-282 (setShaderFogStart/End then ClientHooks.onFogRender as last statement); ref/mc/net/neoforged/neoforge/client/ClientHooks.java:447-459; javap -c/-v of sodium-extra MixinFogRenderer (setupFog TAIL; applyTerrainFog offsets 0-78); MixinDefaultChunkRenderer.java:74 (VoxyFogParameters.current()); VoxyFogParameters.java:57-59; NormalRenderPipeline.java:102-117; roxy/mixin/RoxyFogRendererMixin.java:14 (Roxy also used TAIL).
findings.proposedFix: Make the CUTOUT-time fog independent of later setupFog injections: have VoxyFogEvents record its decision (pushed or not) plus the fog it intends the LODs to see in VoxyFogParameters (e.g. a static `lodFog()` = the post-decision value), and have MixinDefaultChunkRenderer.doRender / the iris MixinLevelRenderer capture use that instead of reading RenderSystem.getShaderFog* at CUTOUT time; additionally (or alternatively) re-assert the push at FogRenderer.setupFog TAIL with a Voxy mixin whose config priority is > 1000 so it runs after sodium-extra's TAIL callback, guarded by the same decision flag.

findings.title: getBoundFramebufferTextures silently falls back to the main render target's depth while Voxy keeps rendering into a different bound framebuffer
findings.detail: When a non-zero framebuffer is bound whose GL_DEPTH_ATTACHMENT is a renderbuffer (or absent), getBoundAttachmentTexture returns 0 and the code substitutes Minecraft.getMainRenderTarget()'s depth/colour textures and size (one-time warning only), but renderOpaque still uses the CURRENTLY bound framebuffer as its output (VoxyRenderSystem.java:278 `oldFB = glGetInteger(GL_DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING)`, later passed as outputFramebuffer to finish). The LODs are then depth-tested/blitted against the main target's depth but written into the other FBO, producing wrong occlusion (LODs drawn through terrain) for any mod that renders the level into its own FBO with a renderbuffer depth. Contract C3 asked to throw/log clearly for fb 0; the fallback for fb != 0 with a non-texture depth attachment is a silent semantic mismatch. Vanilla main target and Iris gbuffers use texture depth attachments (ref RenderTarget.java:118-127), so the user's setup is not affected.
findings.evidence: VoxyRenderSystem.java:454-480 (getBoundFramebufferTextures fallback branch `if (drawFb == 0 || depthTexture == 0)`), :482-488 (getBoundAttachmentTexture returns 0 for non-GL_TEXTURE), :278 (oldFB used as output).
findings.proposedFix: Only fall back to the main render target when drawFb == 0 (or when drawFb == mainTarget.frameBufferId); for any other bound framebuffer without a texture depth attachment log once and skip Voxy's opaque pass for that frame (return null viewport) instead of mixing depth from one FBO with colour output to another.

findings.title: BakedBlockEntityModel was a commented-out file upstream but is now compiled and drags three new vanilla accessor mixins into client.voxy.mixins.json for a feature that is not wired in

The port un-commented it, rewrote it for 1.21.1 and registered minecraft.AccessorCompositeRenderType, minecraft.AccessorCompositeState and minecraft.AccessorEmptyTextureStateShard (client.voxy.mixins.json:6-8) solely so BakedBlockEntityModel.getLayerTextureId compiles, while the class is still not referenced by SoftwareModelTextureBakery (its own header says so). findings.title: Upstream JMH benchmark source set is no longer built: the me.champeau.jmh plugin and jmh {} block were dropped but src/jmh was kept
findings.detail: dev's build.gradle applies `id "me.champeau.jmh" version "0.7.3"` (line 4) and configures `jmh {` (line 413); the ported build.gradle has no JMH plugin and only references sourceSets.main (line 110), so `src/jmh` (still present in the working tree) is neither compiled nor runnable and will rot against the 1.21.1 API. findings.title: PreparedState ThreadLocal is not cleared when VoxyInstance's constructor throws DontCreateInstance (or anything else)
findings.detail: The JEP-447 replacement stores the parsed storage Config in a static ThreadLocal in prepare() and removes it only after super() returns (line 41). When shouldCreateInstance() returns false the super constructor throws DontCreateInstance (VoxyInstance.java:35-37), the private constructor never reaches PREPARED.remove(), and the render thread keeps a stale PreparedState (Config + basePath) until the next prepare() overwrites it. Functionally benign today (VoxyCommon.createInstance catches DontCreateInstance and the next call re-sets the value), but it is a latent leak and a trap for any future caller that instantiates VoxyClientInstance from another thread or reads PREPARED after a failed construction. shouldCreateInstance's `this.config` fallback (line 65) is always null at that point, so it never helps.
findings.proposedFix: Wrap construction in a static factory (e.g. `static VoxyClientInstance create() { try { return new VoxyClientInstance(); } finally { PREPARED.remove(); } }`) and register that with VoxyCommon.setInstanceFactory, or clear the ThreadLocal at the start of prepare().

findings.title: Any FOG_TERRAIN setupFog call from third parties (sodium-extra cloud fog, other fog mods cancelling the event) is classified as the render-distance wall and pushed away
findings.detail: The handler only checks mode == FOG_TERRAIN, FogType.NONE and `end >= max(renderDistance,32)`; it does not know whether the call came from LevelRenderer.renderLevel:966. sodium-extra's MixinLevelRenderer.setupCloudFog lambda (javap: lambda$setupCloudFog$0(Camera, float, boolean, float) -> FogRenderer.setupFog) re-enters setupFog with FOG_TERRAIN for clouds; when its far plane is >= the render distance the cloud fog is pushed to 1e9 (clouds lose their fog band) and VoxyFogParameters.setLastTerrainFog is overwritten with cloud values. Likewise a higher-priority RenderFog subscriber that lowers the far plane below max(rd,32) makes Voxy treat the wall as environmental fog and keep it (LODs fogged out under FOG/FOG_AND_FADE). Cosmetic/fragile rather than crashing; listed separately from FULL-01 because the fix is a different guard.
findings.evidence: VoxyFogEvents.java:72-95; javap of sodium-extra MixinLevelRenderer (setupCloudFog + lambda$setupCloudFog$0) and MixinFogRenderer offset 24-35 (FogOverrideState.isSettingUpCloudFog path).
findings.proposedFix: Only act on the terrain call made by LevelRenderer.renderLevel (e.g. set a flag from a mixin at LevelRenderer.renderLevel CONSTANT "fog"/before the FOG_TERRAIN setupFog invoke and clear it after, or compare `event.getFarPlaneDistance()` against the exact `Math.max(gameRenderer.getRenderDistance(),32)` AND require the call stack/flag), and treat cancelled-by-others events conservatively.
